sourceOfTruth: index.html is canonical. No design tool file exists for this project — there is nothing else to reconcile against.

architecture.motionPrimitives: Global, non-brand-scoped constants (--dur-*, --ease-*, --dist-*, --stagger, --seq). Motion does not vary by brand in this system — this is a deliberate 4th category, not a taxonomy gap. See Phase 1 spec for the reasoning.

boundary.note: The 'tokens only, zero overrides' contract governs the COMPONENT LIBRARY — the reusable system being sold. It does NOT govern the demo harness (the browser-chrome mockup, the token inspector, the stage scaffolding) that exists to SHOW the system. Holding the harness to the contract is a category error. This boundary is declared here so the guardrail reads it from the contract rather than guessing. Drawing this line explicitly is itself the senior distinction — a design system is a bounded, governed contract with a defined edge, not 'all the CSS in the file'.
boundary.harnessException: The harness may use raw hex — it is presentation scaffolding, not part of the token-governed system. Its accessibility is still checked separately (Phase 3 fixed a real AA failure in it), but it is exempt from the token-consumption rule.

never: Never reference a --primitive-* token directly inside a component rule. Components read --semantic-* or --alias-* only — that indirection is what makes zero-override theming structural rather than disciplined.

Never reference a brand name (aurora/ember/atlas) inside a component selector, EXCEPT the existing [data-brand="..."] asset-visibility blocks, which exist specifically to swap per-brand SVG artwork and pattern devices. That exception is documented and closed — do not extend the pattern to anything else.
Never hardcode a hex colour value inside a component rule. All colour must resolve through a token, full stop.

Never introduce a new --semantic-* token without: (1) adding it to this contract, (2) computing its WCAG contrast ratio against every background it will realistically sit on, (3) confirming it clears 4.5:1 for text usage or 3:1 for non-text UI components per WCAG 1.4.11.

Never invent a new variant-naming convention. Every existing variant in this codebase uses a modifier class following the pattern `.component-variantname` (see btn-primary/btn-secondary). New variants must follow the same convention.
always: New interactive components must include :focus-visible using var(--semantic-focus), matching every existing interactive element in this file.
New interactive components with a checked/pressed state must use aria-checked or aria-pressed, matching .ctrl and .bswitch.
Any new animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion — add the selector to the existing @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) block, do not create a second one.

image-hero.purpose: Primary hero band. Subtitle (optional) / Title / Description / CTA row / per-brand media.
image-hero.perBrandAssets: SVG art swapped via [data-brand] + .art-{brand} visibility toggle — the one sanctioned exception to the no-brand-name rule.

cta-section.purpose: Pattern-carrier band. Heading + supporting text over a per-brand background device.
cta-section.perBrandAssets: background pattern swapped via [data-brand] + .p-{brand} visibility toggle — same sanctioned exception as image-hero.

product-card.purpose: Product summary card — media, title, description, price row, badge, CTA.
product-card.note: price-was uses primitive-neutral-400 directly — a pre-existing exception for a struck-through/de-emphasised price, not a violation of the semantic-only rule since it never carries brand meaning. Flagged here so an agent doesn't treat it as a bug to 'fix'.

btn.purpose: Primary interactive action element. The established variant-modifier precedent for the whole system.

variants.btn-primary: background: semantic-action-primary, hover swaps to semantic-action-primary-hover-bg
variants.btn-block: width:100% modifier, combinable with either variant above

btn.a11y: focus-visible with semantic-focus outline — present and correct.

toggle.a11y: uses aria-checked — correct pattern to follow for any new stateful control.

checkbox-radio.purpose: Shared base control, differentiated by modifier class — this is a second real variant precedent alongside btn.

toast.status: PARTIAL — Phase 0 finding. A single hardcoded success-state instance exists. No variant modifier classes exist. Only 2 of 4 needed semantic feedback tokens existed before Phase 1 (success, error); warning and info were added in Phase 1 and are now available and AA-verified.
toast.phase4Task: Extend to 4 variants — toast-success, toast-warning, toast-error, toast-info — following the exact modifier-class convention already established by btn-primary/btn-secondary. Each variant swaps only the border-left colour and .tdot background to its corresponding --semantic-feedback-* token. Do not touch .tclose, .tprog structural rules — only the feedback-colour bindings vary per variant. Do not add a 5th variant, do not rename the base .toast class, do not introduce a new token-naming pattern.
